purpose: Check whether the known-good Gemian boot reports a Type-C controller interrupt failure after a reported left-port-to-Mac baseline and an unconfirmed charger-move window.

observed.i2c0_0x25: fusb301a bound to FUSB301_1; boot log reports IRQ 0x183 (387)
observed.i2c1_0x25: fusb301 bound to FUSB301_0; boot log reports IRQ 0 and request_irq return -22
observed.proc_interrupts: fusb300-eint exists as MT-EINT 3 at IRQ 387, with zero counted interrupts at this snapshot

source_review.finding: fusb301_eint_init returns request_irq's error, but fusb301_i2c_probe ignores that return and returns zero after a later register read. Thus the pinned source permits a bound I2C driver after interrupt setup failed. The live boot log and binding match this pattern, but the source commit is not an exact binary attestation of this boot.

limits: The two I2C devices have no proved mapping to the PDA's physical ports. An interrupt registration failure is not a direct VBUS measurement or proof that charger detection depends on this IRQ. The owner did not confirm a move from the Mac to the known-good charger during either five-minute watch; no charger-response conclusion follows. No I2C register, role, power or radio control was accessed.
